name: Chenaanah
overview: Chenaanah was a male member of the tribe of Benjamin, identified specifically as the son of Bilhan. His mention in Scripture is concise, with no additional personal details or narrative events recorded beyond his lineage. This brief reference situates him within the genealogical records of Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Chenaanah means 'toward Canaan,' reflecting a proper name used in the Old Testament. There is no indication that this name was given directly by God, but it carries a geographic or cultural connotation related to the land of Canaan.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Chenaanah as the son of Bilhan, establishing a clear paternal relationship. Beyond this, no further family connections or relationships are noted in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Chenaanah's significance lies primarily in his inclusion in the genealogical records of the tribe of Benjamin. His mention helps preserve the lineage and heritage of Israel, which is important for understanding God's covenant people. Though not prominent in narrative events, his record contributes to the biblical emphasis on God's faithfulness through generations.
